state:
Ticket SW-88213 | Account: Harbor & Pine Home Goods (Stockwell Growth plan, $86,400/year, renewal April 8, 2026)
Status: open | Priority: P1 (raised from P2) | Linked incident: INC-2291 | Customer since: 2021

--- Message 1 ---
From: Priya Raman <priya.raman@harborandpine.example> (Operations Lead)
To: support@stockwell.example
Date: Mon, Mar 2, 2026, 08:12 UTC
Subject: Every order is showing up twice since last night

Hi Stockwell team,

Since roughly 02:00 UTC every order coming in from our Shopify store appears twice in Stockwell, with two different Stockwell order numbers but the same Shopify order number. Our morning shift at the Columbus warehouse started picking at 06:00 and nobody noticed until 07:30, when a packer found two identical boxes going to the same customer. By then 140 orders had been picked and packed twice.

I have paused picking in Columbus. Can you tell me whether it is safe to resume, and what we should do with the duplicates? Monday is our biggest day: we have about 1,900 orders queued from the weekend.

Thanks,
Priya

--- Message 2 ---
From: Tom Becker <tom.becker@stockwell.example> (Support Engineer)
Date: Mon, Mar 2, 2026, 09:05 UTC

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the detailed report. I have opened ticket SW-88213 at priority P2 and I am looking at your account now. Could you send me three or four examples of duplicated orders (the Shopify order numbers are enough)?

As a workaround, you can switch off automatic order sync under Settings > Channels > Shopify, which stops new duplicates from being created while we investigate. Please do not delete any orders yet; we may need them to trace the problem.

Best,
Tom

--- Message 3 ---
From: Priya Raman
Date: Mon, Mar 2, 2026, 09:40 UTC

Tom,

Examples: #HP-10421, #HP-10422, #HP-10427 and #HP-10433. Each one has two Stockwell orders.

I switched off automatic sync as you suggested, but now no new orders arrive at all, so we are stuck either way. This needs to be treated as a P1. Every hour that Columbus is not picking costs us around $4,000 in overtime later this week, and if we miss the 16:00 UPS pickup, today's orders go out a day late. Please call me at +1 614 555 0182 if that is faster.

Priya

--- Message 4 ---
From: Tom Becker
Date: Mon, Mar 2, 2026, 11:20 UTC

Hi Priya,

I have raised the ticket to P1 and our engineering team has opened incident INC-2291. What we know so far: release 4.18.0 was deployed at 01:45 UTC. During the deploy our webhook endpoint answered slowly, Shopify retried its order webhooks, and the retries were stored as new orders instead of being recognised as repeats. Other merchants are affected as well.

Engineering is writing a script to find and merge the duplicate orders, and a fix is expected later today. Until then you can import new orders manually: in Shopify, export the unfulfilled orders as CSV and upload the file under Orders > Import in Stockwell. Imported orders are not duplicated.

I will update you as soon as the fix is deployed.

Tom

--- Message 5 ---
From: Priya Raman
Date: Mon, Mar 2, 2026, 15:55 UTC

Tom,

The CSV import worked, but it was slow, and we missed the 16:00 UPS pickup for about 600 orders.

It is also worse than we thought. Our Reno warehouse (location RENO-2) never paused, because the alert went only to Columbus, so Reno shipped another 172 orders twice. That makes 312 orders that went out twice in total. We are paying for two sets of labels and, in many cases, losing the second item, because customers do not send it back.

And there is a payment problem: 57 customers were charged twice. Shopify shows two captures for each of those orders, both triggered when Stockwell marked the order as fulfilled. That is $9,870 in duplicate charges. Customers are emailing us and a few have posted about it on Instagram.

Who covers the cost of the duplicate shipments and the refunds?

Priya

--- Message 6 ---
From: Tom Becker
Date: Mon, Mar 2, 2026, 17:30 UTC

Hi Priya,

Update on INC-2291: the fix, release 4.18.1, was deployed at 16:40 UTC. Webhook retries are recognised again, and the cleanup script has merged 1,188 duplicate order records on your account. You can switch automatic sync back on.

About the payments: Stockwell does not process payments itself, but our engineers confirmed that for 57 of your orders Stockwell sent the fulfilment call to Shopify twice, which is what triggered the second capture. So this is on us. I am preparing a list of the 57 orders with both capture IDs so that you can refund the second charge in Shopify.

I have passed your question about the costs to your account manager, Elena Vasquez, who can speak to that.

I am very sorry for the disruption today.

Tom

--- Message 7 ---
From: Marcus Oyelaran <marcus.oyelaran@harborandpine.example> (Chief Financial Officer)
To: Elena Vasquez <elena.vasquez@stockwell.example>
Cc: Priya Raman, Tom Becker
Date: Tue, Mar 3, 2026, 08:02 UTC
Subject: Re: Every order is showing up twice since last night

Elena,

I am writing about yesterday's incident. By our count, it cost Harbor & Pine $31,500: warehouse overtime, 312 duplicate shipments with their labels and lost goods, the work of refunding customers, and chargeback fees on two orders where customers went to their bank instead of waiting for us.

We renew our contract with Stockwell on April 8. We expect Stockwell to cover these direct costs, and we want a written root-cause analysis by Friday, March 6. We are also evaluating Linnworks and Brightpearl, and we have a demo with Brightpearl next week.

I would like a call this week with someone who can make commercial decisions. I do not want to hear about the SLA credit cap.

Marcus Oyelaran
CFO, Harbor & Pine Home Goods

--- Message 8 ---
From: Elena Vasquez <elena.vasquez@stockwell.example> (Account Manager)
Date: Tue, Mar 3, 2026, 09:15 UTC

Marcus, Priya,

I am sorry. Yesterday should not have happened, and I understand why you are looking at alternatives.

I have booked a call for Wednesday, March 4 at 15:00 UTC with our VP of Customer Success, Daniel Cho, who can make commercial decisions. You will have the written root-cause analysis by Friday, March 6.

For transparency: the credit under our SLA (99.9% monthly availability) is capped at 10% of the monthly fee, which is $720 and far below your costs. Daniel and I are preparing a proposal that goes well beyond that, and we will bring it to Wednesday's call.

Elena

--- Internal note (not visible to customer) ---
Author: Kwame Mensah (Engineering, INC-2291 lead)
Date: Tue, Mar 3, 2026, 10:02 UTC

Root cause confirmed. Release 4.18.0 moved the Shopify webhook consumer to the new queue service. The migration renamed the header we use as the idempotency key (X-Shopify-Webhook-Id became X-Shopify-Event-Id in our parser), so the duplicate check never matched. Shopify retried roughly 1,900 webhooks because of the slow 5xx responses during the deploy, and each retry created a new order. The same bug made the fulfilment worker send some fulfilment calls twice, which caused the double payment captures. 23 merchants were affected; Harbor & Pine is by far the worst (1,188 of 1,904 duplicate orders and all 57 double captures). 4.18.1 restores the old header name and adds a regression test. The postmortem draft is due Thursday.

--- Internal note (not visible to customer) ---
Author: Tom Becker
Date: Tue, Mar 3, 2026, 10:30 UTC

Priya reports that Reno (RENO-2) still shows 9 duplicate pick lists. I asked engineering to re-run the cleanup script for that location. The list of the 57 double captures is attached to the ticket.

--- Message 9 ---
From: Priya Raman
Date: Tue, Mar 3, 2026, 11:45 UTC

Tom,

The 9 Reno pick lists are gone, thanks. Automatic sync has been back on since 08:00 and today's orders look clean in both warehouses.

We have already refunded 41 of the 57 double-charged customers ourselves from Shopify, and we will do the other 16 today using your list. Two customers had already filed chargebacks, which cost us $15 each on top of the refund.

We will keep an eye on things until Wednesday's call.

Priya
